title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page (typescript p. 35, upside down in the scan) of a uniqueness and existence argument for a canonical arrow ψ(S,Z,Y,X). The arrow is attached to a smooth triple Z ⊂ Y ⊂ X over a base S. The surrounding pages, about Tannakian and Hodge filtered crystals, are unrelated manuscript notes filed in the same folder.

The context is most plausibly the construction of a Gysin or fundamental-class isomorphism (purity) for a smooth pair (Z,X) of codimension c in a cohomology theory such as de Rham, crystalline or étale. The arrow is first defined in low codimension, then extended to higher codimension by factoring Z ⊂ Y ⊂ X.

Step 1. After a base change S' → S, set ψ(S,Z,Y,X) = ξ∘η∘φ(Z,Y). This is a composite of the arrow for (Z,Y) with transitivity and identification maps. ψ is local on X and commutes with base change.

Step 2. If (Z,X) is smooth of codimension c > 1, one can, locally on X, insert Y with 0 < codim(Y,X) < c. It therefore suffices to show ψ is independent of Y. Independence gives uniqueness in codimension c. Existence then follows by descent, gluing the local definitions.

Step 3. Reduction to codimension 1. If codim(Y,X) > 1, one can locally find a smooth W with Y ⊂ W ⊂ X and codim(W,X) = 1. A transitivity diagram chase, left to the reader, then reduces to comparing two intermediate Y's that are both hypersurfaces.

Step 4. Homotopy (deformation) argument. Take Y_0 = {f_0 = 0} and Y_1 = {f_1 = 0}, both containing Z. Work over S̲ = Spec O_S[t] (the affine line over S). On X̲ = X ×_S S̲, consider the hypersurface Y̲ : (f_1 − f_0)t + f_0 = 0. It contains Z̲ and specializes to Y_0 at t = 0 and to Y_1 at t = 1. The claim being started is that Y̲/S̲ is smooth at points above Z, or above some neighbourhood. This would let one compare ψ for Y_0 and Y_1 via the family over the affine line, using base-change compatibility at t = 0 and t = 1. The page breaks off mid-sentence.
errors: Gap/caution: the family f_t = (1−t)f_0 + t f_1 is smooth along Z̲ only where the image of df_t in the conormal of Z is nonzero. If df_1 ≡ λ df_0 mod I_Z^2 with λ ≠ 1, this fails at t = 1/(1−λ), possibly a point between 0 and 1. So one must restrict to an open subset of the affine line containing t = 0 and t = 1 (or change f_1 by a unit). One also needs an argument that a base-change-compatible arrow over such an open is 'constant' in t. The visible text does not address this; it may be handled on the next typescript page, which is not available.

Minor typographical slips in the original: 'cet situation' (for 'cette situation'), 'indépendant' (for 'indépendante'), 'définis chaque' (for 'chacun'), and a missing symbol in 'l'unicité de [ψ] pour codimension c'.

ideas.what: Define a canonical (Gysin/fundamental-class-type) arrow in codimension c by factoring through an intermediate smooth subscheme. Prove independence of the factorization, then glue by descent.
ideas.modern_name: Construction of Gysin maps / cycle classes by dévissage on codimension and transitivity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck school (SGA 4 XVIII, SGA 4½ 'Cycle' by Deligne; Berthelot for crystalline; Hartshorne/Grothendieck for coherent duality)
ideas.where_published: Similar arguments appear in SGA 4 (purity, trace) and SGA 4½ Cycle; exact source of this typescript unsure

ideas.what: Comparison of two hypersurfaces through Z by the linear interpolation f_t = (f_1 − f_0)t + f_0 over the affine line, using base-change compatibility at t = 0 and t = 1.
ideas.modern_name: A^1-homotopy / deformation trick for independence of choices

deep.surprise_reason: This is a fragment of a polished typescript giving a standard dévissage-plus-homotopy proof that a Gysin-type arrow is independent of choices. It is routine technique and was likely incorporated into some published or circulated text. Nothing new is visible.
transcription_corrections: The page is printed upside down; the transcription is otherwise essentially faithful to the image.
The struck-out heading '2X' is probably a struck-out section number or symbol before 'S' → S'.
